summary: Paul Tillich was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle, and Breslau (PhD ~1911). He held professorships at Dresden, Leipzig, Frankfurt, Union Theological Seminary (1933-1955), Harvard (1955-1962), and Chicago (1962-1965).

Paul W. Kroll is a sinologist who studied at the University of Michigan (~1971-1976). He spent his career at the University of Colorado, serving as Associate Professor of Chinese (~1979-1990) and continuing on the faculty through 2018.

Paul Williams is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his BA at Sussex and his DPhil at Oxford. He served as a fellow at Wadham College and spent the bulk of his career at the University of Bristol (~1978-2011).

Paul de Lagarde worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies. He studied under Friedrich Rückert and at Berlin and Halle, later holding academic posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1851-1852) and Göttingen (~1869-1891).

Paula Kane Robinson Arai works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at Waseda, Kalamazoo College, and Harvard (PhD 1993), she held faculty posts at Vanderbilt, Carleton College, and Louisiana State University, becoming a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies in 2023.

Paulinus of St. Bartholomew was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Collegio San Pancrazio (~1774-1776). He served on the Malabar Mission (1776-1789) and later held posts with the Congregation of the Index and the Pontifical Urban University in 1800.

Pe Maung Tin was a scholar of Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology who studied at Rangoon, Calcutta, and Oxford. He served as professor and principal at the University of Rangoon (1912; 1937-1946) and principal of the University of Adult Education (1947).
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at the University of Sunderland, studying under Peter Harvey.

Pei-jung Wu is a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her BA from National Taiwan University and completed her PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2002 under Donald F. McCallum.

Pema Bhum is a tibetologist who previously served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University, and was director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003-2009).

Pema Chödrön is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Sarah Lawrence College and UC Berkeley. A disciple of Chögyam Trungpa and other teachers, she directed the Boulder Shambhala Center and served as director and abbess at Gampo Abbey.
Pema Kunzang Tendzin studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Pema Tekchok Loden studied under Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Khenpo Shenga.
Pema Tekchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He also taught Shechen Gyaltsab and Khenpo Shenga.
Pema Tsering is a tibetologist who studied under Khenpo Shenga and served as an editorial consultant at the University of Bonn (attested 1982).
Pema Vajra 01 studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Khenpo Shenga, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Pema Wangchok Gyelpo studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Khakyab Dorje, and Khenpo Shenga. He taught Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Khenpo Shenga.
Penghao Sun is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He pursued studies under teachers including Leonard van der Kuijp, Qingying Chen, and Weirong Shen.
Penor 02 was both a teacher and a student of Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye as well as Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Penor Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Palyul Monastery and under teachers including Thubten Chökyi Dawa and Dilgo Khyentse. He founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in 1978 and taught numerous students.
